title: Thy Name Be Hallowed Evermore
description: Thy Name Be Hallowed Evermore in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 100 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Lord's Prayer”, where the book credits them to a Moravian source.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy name be hal-lowed ev-er-more; O God! thy king-dom come with power! Thy will be done, and day by day, Give us our dail-y bread, we pray:

lines: O God! thy kingdom come with power!
Thy will be done, and day by day,
Give us our daily bread, we pray:
Lord! evermore to us be given
The living bread that came from heaven:
Water of life on us bestow,
Thou art the Source, the Fountain thou.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
